awd_abstract_narration:
This conference will convene leaders from government and the quantum industry to strengthen public-private collaboration in quantum information science and technology (QIST). QIST encompasses emerging technologies in quantum computing, sensing, and networking that promise transformative advances across sectors such as national security, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing. By identifying shared priorities and actionable strategies, the event aims to accelerate the transition of research into real-world applications. The resulting report will guide future investments and partnerships, supporting U.S. leadership in quantum innovation, economic growth, and national security.

Held in Washington D.C., the conference will bring together federal agencies, quantum developers, and commercial end users to explore strategies for identifying science and technology barriers faced by industry and methods for engaging government and government-funded researchers to accelerate innovation. Sessions will include keynotes, panels, and breakout discussions on topics such as workforce development, partnership models, and methodologies for identifying industry’s technology needs in quantum computing, sensing, and networking. A final report will summarize findings for broad dissemination.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project supported a workshop organized by SRI International and the Quantum Economic Development Consortium (QED-C) on January 23, 2026. The workshop convened participants from government and industry with expertise in quantum computing, technology commercialization, and regulatory navigation, as well as representatives from potential end-user sectors including finance, healthcare, and defense. Participants discussed how government agencies that fund research can better engage with industry to transfer quantum computing research results to practical applications.

Workshop activities included keynote remarks that addressed government and private investment in quantum computing, as well as examples of partnership models that could inform future quantum collaborations. Industry stakeholders and prospective end users participated in panel discussions to outline how quantum computing might demonstrate measurable impact for major industries in the near term. During small-group sessions, participants identified features of successful quantum partnerships.

Participants described a continuing gap between progress in quantum computing research and evidence of value to potential users. They emphasized that adoption will require measurable evidence that quantum approaches improve on existing computing methods and identified performance measures, benchmarks, and validation methods as priorities for future research and development. They also identified quantum algorithms and methods for detecting and correcting computational errors as promising areas for collaborative work because progress in these areas could benefit multiple technologies and users.

Participants examined challenge and prize programs, research centers and consortia, shared research infrastructure, and coordination across federal agencies. Rather than selecting a single preferred model, participants identified common design considerations that apply across different approaches. These included clearly defined problems, participant roles, incentives, intellectual property terms, flexible participation, and measures of progress.

The project produced a public report, Advancing Quantum Computing toward Practical Applications through Government-Industry Engagement, which documents the workshop findings, potential partnership models, and design considerations for future government-industry partnerships. The workshop also allowed participants to compare their differing needs, priorities, and roles. By making these findings publicly available, the report can inform future research programs and collaborations. The report is available at https://quantumconsortium.org/publication/advancing-quantum-computing-toward-practical-applications-through-government-industry-engagement/.
